description: A signal driven past a voltage range and folded or wrapped back inside it, in 2HP

params.text: Amplifies the input, 1x fully counter-clockwise to 10x fully clockwise, which is what drives it past the range
Attenuates and inverts the gain CV between -100% and +100%, and comes up at 0%
Leans the signal towards the lower or the upper half of the range, so the folding happens mostly on one side
Attenuates and inverts the bias CV between -100% and +100%, and comes up at 0%
Switches what the Bias knob does: an offset applied to the signal, or a different gain on the upper and lower halves of the range
Chooses what happens past the range: Fld turns the excess back down from the limit, Wrp carries it round to the other limit
Sets the range the signal is held inside: -5V to 5V or 0V to 10V

inputs.text: Moves the gain, 10V covering the knob's full travel at full trim
Moves the bias, 10V covering the knob's full travel at full trim

outputs.text: Carries the folded or wrapped signal, always inside the chosen range

notes: with the gain at 1x and no bias, a signal already inside the range comes out unchanged; the module does nothing until something pushes past a limit
driving the signal far past the range folds or wraps it more than once, which is where the complicated shapes come from
menu: Oversampling: Single, 2x — runs the fold at twice the sample rate, which is worth it on audio and off unless you turn it on
Clipping range — clamps every output to the range chosen, -12V to 12V unless you change it, and Off lets the output run to any voltage
Process quality: Audio, High, Balanced, Low, Very low — sets how often the module runs its algorithm, from every cycle down to every 256th; below Balanced a 1ms trigger can be missed

inputs.0:
±10V · continuous · one channel only

unpatched it reads 0V; a negative voltage subtracts from the knob; the knob and this input are summed and the total held to 1 to 10V.
inputs.1:
±10V · continuous · one channel only

unpatched it reads 0V; the knob and this input are summed and the total held to ±1V.
